title: US Market Outlook: Jobs Report & AI Earnings This Week
summary: US stocks face a big test this week: Friday's jobs report plus Broadcom and Palo Alto earnings. Here is the economic agenda and stocks to watch.
body_markdown:
Beyond the headline Non-Farm Payrolls number, you will also want to watch the unemployment rate and wage growth. All three feed directly into rate expectations.


Interestingly, expectations for the Fed have shifted more hawkish since the Jackson Hole symposium. The CME FedWatch tool at one point showed the odds of a September Fed Rate hike rising to around 60 percent, up from 35 percent.


That mix of a softening labor market and a more hawkish Fed is exactly what makes Friday's report so important. A single print can move rate expectations within minutes.


The Fed meeting on September 15-16 has not happened yet, but expectations are already forming now. So every economic release this week will be read as a clue to that decision.


Beyond the jobs data, markets will also track releases like job openings and manufacturing activity through the week. The next CPI print is not due until September 11, so this week's focus stays firmly on the labor side.


Manufacturing and services activity data will also hint at the economy's broader health. A slowdown there could reinforce the narrative that the US economy is cooling.


One more thing keeping investors cautious is elevated US bond yields. The 30-year Treasury yield recently touched its highest level in nearly two decades.


High bond yields also tend to pressure the valuations of growth stocks, especially in tech. That is why strong economic data plus elevated yields can act as a double headwind for AI names.


If you want to prepare early, check the full data schedule on the[Gotrade Economic Calendar](https://www.heygotrade.com/app-download/) .


## Stocks to Watch


Tech earnings season rolls on, and two big names take the spotlight this week. Both will serve as a gauge of how real demand in the AI space really is.


[Palo Alto Networks (PANW)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/panw/) is set to report after the close on Tuesday, September 1. The focus is whether the AI story in cybersecurity is actually driving revenue growth.


[Broadcom (AVGO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/avgo/) follows after the close on Wednesday, September 2. Its AI chip revenue is expected to reach around 15.23 billion US dollars, including custom chips for[Google (GOOG)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/goog/) ,[Meta (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) , and OpenAI.


Strong results from both could reinforce AI's market leadership. Disappointing numbers, however, could trigger a rotation out of tech.


For context, the chip sector was rattled in late August. In a single session, Micron fell about 5.8 percent, while AMD and Broadcom slid more than 3 and 2 percent respectively.


Sentiment in the chip sector has clearly been choppy.[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) recently jumped about 8.7 percent after its results beat expectations and it guided to strong revenue growth.


That surge helped ease worries about the durability of the AI trade. Even so, other semiconductor names like[AMD](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) and[Micron (MU)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) remain prone to sharp swings, so they are worth watching.


The price reaction to Broadcom and Palo Alto results will be an important tell. A positive response would signal that AI optimism is still firmly supporting tech.


Beyond those two heavyweights, moves in other semiconductor names are worth tracking too. The sector often acts as a barometer for risk appetite toward the broader AI theme.


## Market Sentiment


Broadly, the AI trade is still the market's main engine. Nvidia's solid results have helped keep investor optimism toward tech intact.


Major indexes like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are still sitting near their highs. That signals risk appetite has not truly faded.


Still, several factors are capping the upside. Historically, September has often been the weakest month for the S&P 500, and that is enough to keep some investors cautious.


A hawkish Fed, high bond yields, and a softening labor market all add to the caution. These threads converge on Friday's jobs report, which can shift direction fast.


Risk appetite will also lean heavily on tech earnings. The AI theme has been the main pillar behind the indexes' gains through 2026 so far.


That means Volatility could pick up, especially around the data release. For you, this is less about guessing direction and more about being ready for two-way moves.


For long-term investors, a seasonal pullback like this can actually be a chance to rebalance. Gradually averaging into positions helps cushion the impact of short-term Volatility.


We suggest focusing on risk management and avoiding large positions right before major data. Watch the reaction to Broadcom and Palo Alto earnings as an early signal of risk appetite in tech.


What is clear is that this week calls for patience and discipline, not impulsive reactions. The goal is to understand the catalysts, not to chase every price move.
